base_instruction: You are a helpful office catering assistant. Help the user plan a catered lunch for their team's all-hands quarterly meeting. Track attendees, their dietary needs, and any changes to the guest list. When asked to evaluate menu items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we've got our quarterly all-hands meeting next Thursday and I need to sort out the catered lunch. Can you help me figure out what to order?

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
Cannot eat any products containing these grains

constraints.value: Cannot eat shellfish or shellfish-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Dev ate shrimp at the holiday party and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Shrimp reaction with throat swelling + EpiPen → severe shellfish allergy
Shellfish allergy → avoid all shellfish and shellfish-derived ingredients

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots)
inference_chain: Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Jain diet → no root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots) due to ahimsa

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw fish or undercooked seafood
constraints.surface_form: Tomoko just announced she's pregnant, about 14 weeks along
inference_chain: Pregnant → dietary restrictions for food safety
Pregnancy → avoid raw fish and undercooked seafood (listeria/parasites risk)

constraints.value: Cannot eat high-carb foods — no bread, pasta, rice, sugar, starchy items
constraints.surface_form: Our CFO Linda is dropping in, she's been doing strict keto for months

hidden_state.value: You are an office manager planning a catered lunch for a quarterly all-hands meeting. You will introduce the team, share their backgrounds and dietary situations, then update the guest list as people drop out or join. At the end you will share a specific menu and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be — you genuinely want the assistant to catch them.

You are a calm, organized office manager. You relay updates about colleagues in third person ('Rachel told me...', 'Dev just pinged me...'). You never express frustration even when plans change. You treat each update as normal workplace coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: Hey, we've got our quarterly all-hands meeting next Thursday and I need to sort out the catered lunch. Can you help me figure out what to order?

There's eight of us confirmed: me, Rachel, Dev, Priya, Marcus, Tomoko, and the two interns Sam and Jordan. Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease last year. Dev ate shrimp at the holiday party and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen. And Priya is Jain, from Gujarat

aims.success_criteria: Agent responds about serviceware without losing constraint state

aims.description: OK so I found this place that does corporate catering. Here's what I'm thinking of ordering: chicken Caesar wraps, miso-glazed salmon poke bowls, mushroom and pesto flatbread, Thai peanut noodle salad, fruit and cheese platter, edamame hummus with pita chips. Any issues?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: chicken Caesar wraps problematic (wrap=gluten for Rachel, chicken=meat for Priya); salmon poke bowls problematic (raw fish for Tomoko, fish for Priya); mushroom and pesto flatbread problematic (flatbread=gluten for Rachel, pesto typically contains garlic for Priya); Thai peanut noodle salad problematic (noodles=high carb for Linda, likely contains garlic for Priya); fruit and cheese platter is fine for everyone; edamame hummus with pita chips has hidden issue (pita=gluten for Rachel, standard hummus contains garlic for Priya)
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 menu items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Current attendees: user, Rachel (celiac→no gluten), Priya (Jain→no meat/fish/eggs/root vegetables including garlic and onion), Tomoko (pregnant→no raw fish), Linda (strict keto→no high-carb), Marcus (absent but wants a plate saved, no stated restrictions), Sam, Jordan. Dev is fully absent (no plate). Analysis: (1) Chicken Caesar wraps — wrap is wheat flour (Rachel celiac), chicken is meat (Priya Jain). (2) Miso-glazed salmon poke bowls — raw fish unsafe for Tomoko (pregnant), fish violates Priya's Jain diet. (3) Mushroom and pesto flatbread — flatbread is wheat (Rachel celiac), pesto standardly contains garlic (Priya Jain no root vegetables). (4) Thai peanut noodle salad — noodles are high-carb (Linda keto), Thai peanut sauce/noodle dishes typically contain garlic (Priya Jain). (5) Fruit and cheese platter — fine for everyone currently attending. (6) Edamame hummus with pita chips — pita is wheat (Rachel celiac), and traditional hummus contains garlic (Priya Jain). The hidden ingredient trap: pesto contains garlic (problematic for Priya) and hummus contains garlic (problematic for Priya) — these are not obvious from the item names.
required_elements: Chicken Caesar wraps are problematic: the wrap contains gluten (Rachel has celiac) AND chicken is meat (Priya is Jain)
Miso-glazed salmon poke bowls are problematic: raw fish is unsafe for Tomoko (pregnant) AND fish violates Priya's Jain diet
Mushroom and pesto flatbread is problematic: flatbread contains gluten (Rachel has celiac) AND pesto typically contains garlic which is a root vegetable (Priya is Jain)
Thai peanut noodle salad is problematic: noodles are high-carb (Linda is on strict keto) AND the dish typically contains garlic (Priya is Jain)
Fruit and cheese platter is fine for all current attendees
Edamame hummus with pita chips is problematic: pita contains gluten (Rachel has celiac) AND hummus typically contains garlic (Priya is Jain)
Agent does NOT flag any shellfish concern for Dev since Dev is fully absent and not getting a plate
forbidden_elements: Flagging shellfish as a concern (Dev is fully absent, not even getting a saved plate)
Saying Tomoko cannot eat cooked fish (pregnancy restriction is specifically about raw/undercooked fish)
Saying the fruit and cheese platter is problematic for anyone currently attending
Treating Linda's keto as eliminating the cheese platter (cheese is keto-friendly)
Over-generalizing Priya's Jain diet to exclude mushrooms (mushrooms are not root vegetables and are generally accepted in Jain diet)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and hidden ingredient inference. Key challenges: (1) Priya is Jain → no meat/fish/eggs/root vegetables — the root vegetable restriction means garlic is forbidden, which is a HIDDEN ingredient in pesto and hummus (the hidden ingredient trap). (2) Tomoko's pregnancy is announced mid-conversation → agent must infer raw fish restriction. (3) Dev fully exits (no plate) → his shellfish allergy is completely removed from consideration. (4) Marcus exits but wants a plate saved → his constraints (none stated) still apply to saved food. (5) Linda joins late with keto → high-carb items are problematic for her. (6) The fruit and cheese platter is the clearly-fine item. (7) The pesto-contains-garlic and hummus-contains-garlic are the hidden ingredient traps requiring multi-step inference (pesto→basil+pine nuts+parmesan+garlic+olive oil→garlic is root vegetable→Priya cannot eat). The over-generalization trap is that mushrooms are NOT root vegetables in Jain classification, so mushroom flatbread's problem is the bread and pesto, not the mushroom itself.

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
